html:
The Sana'a manuscript is one of the oldest known copies of the Quran, found in 1972 among thousands of old parchment fragments hidden in the roof of the Great Mosque of Sana'a.

It is a palimpsest: an older text was washed off and a newer one written over it. The lower text, read with ultraviolet light, dates by radiocarbon to the first decades of Islam. It differs from the standard text in small ways, in wording and the order of some passages.

Scholars use it to study how the Quran was written down and how the standard version, attributed to the caliph Uthman, spread. It is one of the most important finds for the early history of Islam.
sum: The Sana'a manuscript is one of the oldest known copies of the Quran, found in 1972 among thousands of old parchment fragments hidden in the roof of the Great Mosque of Sana'a.
